stories.title: Canada puts $800M Griffon helicopter upgrade on hold over technical 'complexity'
stories.summary: The federal government has suspended the Royal Canadian Air Force's $800-million Griffon helicopter life-extension program amid technical problems and growing concerns over cost and complexity. The pause raises fresh questions about whether all 82 aircraft will be upgraded as Ottawa weighs a multibillion-dollar alternative (CBC reports a figure on the order of $18 billion).
stories.connection: DIRECT procurement-anomaly hit and the most investigation-relevant story of the scan. This is a FOURTH defence-procurement signal in a fortnight, broadening the 'procurement velocity/distortion' cluster from sole-sourcing and rushed competitions to a troubled-program pause/pivot: a marquee life-extension program stalls on cost/complexity while Ottawa weighs a far larger new acquisition. Maps to procurement_anomalies.json and arms_pipeline_dossier.json, with arms_grover_decisionmakers.json and revolving_door_analysis.json for vendor/industry ties, and defense_nexus.json. Sits against Carney's stated 4%-of-GDP-by-2029 defence target (the rising-budget backdrop tracked in brief_20260626). Confirm the $800M program scope, the 82-aircraft figure and the alternative's price tag against published DND/PSPC records before any use.

stories.title: Senior leaders of Edmonton-based infantry battalion reinstated after investigation
stories.summary: The Department of National Defence has reinstated two leaders of a respected Edmonton battalion days after announcing they had been removed pending an investigation. The rapid removal-then-reinstatement raises questions about what triggered the action and how the review was resolved.
stories.connection: Military command-accountability / process-integrity data point mapping to cfnis_command_dossier.json and cfnis_accountability_dossier.json. A fast removal-then-reinstatement of named-but-unspecified senior officers is exactly the kind of opaque chain-of-command disciplinary event the CFNIS/military-justice mapping tracks. Lower direct weight than a named-subject finding, but worth logging: watch for what the investigation concerned, who ordered the removal and reinstatement, and whether any public statement of reasons follows.

stories.title: Liberals claim to be the party of law and order now -- inside the party's about-face on crime
stories.summary: After years of criminal-justice reform that included a lighter touch for some offenders, the federal Liberal government has done an about-face over the past year, enacting stricter policies to tamp down on crime rates that have become a political liability in vote-rich regions.
stories.connection: Criminal-justice policy-reversal / governance signal mapping to enforcement_followthrough.json (the promise-vs-delivery gap pattern) and the broader justice-accountability domain. Relevant as a policy-direction marker rather than a named-subject hit: a publicly acknowledged reversal invites scrutiny of which earlier reforms are being walked back, what the evidence base is, and whether the shift is driven by data or electoral exposure (the Alberta referendum / vote-rich-region framing). Medium investigative weight; carry forward to track specific legislative/regulatory changes enacted under the new posture.

stories.title: Construction set to start on first road to Ontario's Ring of Fire mineral deposit
stories.summary: An environmental assessment has been approved for a road the Ontario government calls vital to accessing critical minerals in the Ring of Fire, which Premier Doug Ford says will add $22 billion to the economy and create 70,000 jobs. The report notes concerns expressed about the project.
stories.connection: Critical-minerals / expedited-infrastructure signal with an Indigenous-consent dimension, extending the northern-megaproject fast-track thread opened in brief_20260626 (the Building Canada Act 'projects of national interest' push). Maps to indigenous_accountability_dossier.json and indigenous_grover_decisionmakers.json. A high-value access road into contested First Nations territory, framed by large economic numbers, is the classic fast-track-without-full-consent risk pattern. Watch for which First Nations consented or objected, the proponents/contractors who benefit, and any litigation over the environmental-assessment approval.

stories.title: Ottawa adds retired judge Corrine Sparks to diversity council after pushback over membership
stories.summary: The first Nova Scotian of African descent appointed to that province's judiciary, now retired, is joining the federal government's newly formed Advisory Council on Rights, Equality and Inclusion -- after scathing criticism of Ottawa for initially omitting a Black representative.
stories.connection: Governance / appointments-process data point with a judicial-adjacent subject (a retired judge), mapping loosely to judicial_accountability_dossier.json and the public-appointments domain. The investigative angle is the process failure that required correction: a federal advisory body stood up without a Black member, reversed only after public pressure. Medium-low weight; relevant as an appointments-integrity signal rather than a misconduct finding.

stories.title: Carney says donor list for 24 Sussex restoration will be public (now confirmed, with media tour)
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney confirmed the national fundraising campaign to refurbish 24 Sussex Drive will cap donations and publish the donor list for transparency. Media were given a behind-the-scenes tour of the uninhabitable residence; a design competition is also planned.
stories.connection: Public-spending / donor-transparency data point, now CONFIRMED (carried from brief_20260626). The donor list itself, once published, is the actionable artifact: cross-reference named private donors against public_figure_intelligence.json and contributions_analysis.json for any influence/access pattern, and log against officer_of_parliament_findings.json (expense-scrutiny domain). Medium weight; flag to revisit on donor-list release and at design-competition award.

stories.title: B.C. launches probe into StubHub over World Cup resale ticket fiasco
stories.summary: British Columbia's attorney general announced an inquiry into ticket reseller StubHub, days after a CBC News investigation revealed a mass failure and cancellation of thousands of FIFA World Cup tickets across host cities in Canada and North America.
stories.connection: Consumer-protection / regulatory-accountability data point. Lower direct federal-mission weight (provincial AG, private platform), but on-theme as a journalism-triggered-enforcement example: a CBC investigation prompting a formal state inquiry. Logs to enforcement_followthrough.json as a positive follow-through data point (the gap pattern's counter-example). Worth watching for whether the inquiry produces enforceable findings.
